title: Using AI-assisted development to bring my creature designs to life in BIOBOND: HELIX — Field Notes #002
author: Studio_Red_Coin
selftext:
I've been working on an indie creature-raising RPG called **BIOBOND: HELIX**, and one of my favorite parts of development lately has been finding ways to bring the creatures I've designed beyond static concept art.

This is Slyter — a Steel-type creature featured in the latest episode of my in-game-inspired series, *Field Notes*.

For this episode, I wanted to create something that felt less like a traditional creature showcase and more like a glimpse into an actual living world. We started with the creature's concept and visual references, then used AI-assisted generation and tools like Minimax H3 to help develop the scenes, action, and presentation around it.

The goal wasn't simply to generate something cool, but to maintain the creature's identity while making it feel like it actually belongs in the world of BIOBOND.

I've been experimenting with combining my own creature designs, concept references, AI-assisted visuals, and traditional editing into something that feels closer to a small animated production than a typical development screenshot.

It's been an interesting process figuring out where these tools are most useful — especially when you already have a specific vision for a character and want to push that vision further without losing its identity.

This is a short clip from the episode. Slyter definitely isn't one to mess around with.

BIOBOND: HELIX is an indie creature-raising RPG currently in development. I'm building a world where raising creatures is only one part of a much larger ecosystem of activities, adventures, competitions, battles, and exploration.

I'd love to hear what other indie developers are doing with AI-assisted art, animation, video, and storytelling in their projects. It's been fascinating watching what this space is becoming.

**Field Notes #002 — Slyter: The Steel Shinobi**
